deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematical derivations. It is part of Hilbert's teaching or study plan ('Studienplan / Lehrplan'). The plan arranges university mathematics into three parallel series of three items each:
- 1-3: Analysis and function theory.
- 1'-3': Number theory and algebra.
- 1''-3'': Geometry and mechanics.

The next page (which logically precedes this one) lists 1, 2, 3, 1', 2', 3' and 1''. This page continues the third series:
- 2'' Analytic geometry: quadratic curves and surfaces, algebraic configurations ('algebraische Gebilde'), curved lines and surfaces (differential geometry).
- 3'' Mechanics: analytical mechanics, potential theory in space, hydrodynamics, electricity, magnetism and light, acoustics and heat, probability calculus.

Hilbert then comments that 3 and 3' (special functions, and algebraic number fields) are the goals ('Ziele') of the plan. They come into close connection as branches that, in 'glorious union' (he struck out 'inniger', more intimate), form the true nodal point where all ideas and lines of thought of the science converge and where new life sprouts. This is a programmatic statement of the unity of mathematics. It matches the meeting of elliptic and modular functions with algebraic number theory (complex multiplication, class fields), which later became Hilbert's 12th problem and the Zahlbericht.

Next he begins a didactic section: in university teaching three points are in the foreground. Point 1) is connection to school knowledge, hence as few prerequisites as possible. Under it, item a: differential and integral calculus, from which three branches lead out: function theory of a real variable, functions of a complex variable, and mechanics.

The previous page continues this section:
- b: algebra, branching into elimination theory, invariant theory and number fields.
- c: geometry, its axioms, topology and higher geometry.
- Point 2: training future teachers.
- Point 3: keeping the scientific standpoint, stating presuppositions such as the continuum explicitly as axioms.

There is nothing to compute.

results.what: Programmatic curriculum dividing mathematics into analysis, algebra/number theory, and geometry/mechanics (each in three stages). Special functions (3) and algebraic number fields (3') are identified as converging goals and the 'nodal point' of all mathematics.
results.modern_name: Hilbert's view of the unity of mathematics; the link between modular/elliptic functions and algebraic number theory (complex multiplication, Kronecker's Jugendtraum, Hilbert's 12th problem)
results.usually_credited_to: Kronecker (Jugendtraum, 1880) for the mathematical link; Hilbert's own unity-of-mathematics rhetoric is well documented (1900 Paris address, Zahlbericht preface 1897)

results.what: Didactic principles for university teaching: connect to school knowledge, minimize prerequisites, start from calculus and branch out.
results.usually_credited_to: Hilbert's teaching notes are discussed in Hilbert scholarship (e.g. Rowe, Corry, Toepell)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a curriculum and teaching-philosophy page with no mathematics. Its emphasis on the unity of mathematics, and on the meeting of special-function theory with algebraic number fields, matches Hilbert's well-known published views (Zahlbericht preface, 1900 address). It is mildly interesting as an early, private formulation of that programme.
